title: E-Commerce Payment Systems
part: Part B — Cyber Safety and E-Commerce

blocks.html: After studying this chapter you will be able to:

items.html: explain what an electronic payment system is and what makes a good one
describe the parties involved in an online card payment and the role of a payment gateway
explain cards, net banking, UPI, wallets, NEFT, RTGS, IMPS and other payment methods used in India
compare these payment methods
use digital payments safely and know what to do if something goes wrong

blocks.html: An online shop is of no use unless customers can pay it. An electronic payment system (e-payment system) lets money move from the buyer to the seller digitally, without cash or cheques.
Definition: An e-payment system is a way of paying for goods and services electronically, using cards, bank accounts, mobile phones or digital wallets over a network.

blocks.text: Features of a good e-payment system

rows: Protects against theft and fraud (encryption, PIN, OTP)
Easy to use on phones and computers
Money moves in seconds or minutes
Accepted by many shops and websites
Every transaction has a reference number for checking and disputes

lessons.title: 9.2 Who is involved in an online card payment?

rows: The customer's bank that issued the card and approves or declines the payment
The merchant's bank that receives the money
Connects the banks and sets rules: RuPay (India's own, by NPCI), Visa, Mastercard and others
Secure software service that collects payment details on the website, encrypts them and passes them to the network; tells the website whether the payment succeeded

blocks.html: Steps of a card payment: customer enters card details → gateway encrypts and forwards them → card network sends them to the issuing bank → issuing bank asks for an OTP (extra authentication) → bank approves and blocks the amount → approval returns to the merchant → order confirmed → money is settled to the merchant's bank later.
The customer pays in cash (or by UPI) when the parcel arrives. It builds trust for first-time online shoppers but is costly and risky for sellers.

rows: Money is taken from your bank account immediately
You borrow from the bank up to a credit limit and pay later
Cannot spend more than your balance
Interest is charged if the bill is not paid in full by the due date
Used for ATM withdrawal and shopping
Used for shopping, EMIs and bookings

blocks.html: A card has a 16-digit number, expiry date and a 3-digit CVV on the back. Online card payments in India need an additional OTP or PIN. Since October 2022, merchants must store a token instead of your card number (Chapter 8).
The customer logs into their bank's website from the merchant's checkout page, using the bank's user ID, password and OTP, and approves the payment directly from the account.
UPI was launched in 2016 by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). It links bank accounts to mobile apps and allows instant transfers 24 × 7.

blocks.caption: Figure 9.1 · The journey of a UPI payment

items.html: UPI ID / VPA (Virtual Payment Address) — an address such as riya@okbank that stands for your account; you need not share your account number and IFSC.
UPI PIN — a 4- or 6-digit secret number needed to approve every payment you send.
QR code payments — scan the shop's QR code, enter the amount and PIN.
Collect request — a request from someone asking you to pay; approving it with your PIN sends your money, so check before approving.
UPI Lite — small payments without entering the PIN each time, from a small preloaded balance.
UPI 123PAY — UPI for basic feature phones (without internet).
UPI AutoPay — automatic recurring payments such as subscriptions or SIPs, with your one-time approval.

blocks.html: A digital wallet (prepaid payment instrument) stores money loaded from a bank or card, to pay quickly at shops and websites. Wallets have spending limits set by RBI and need KYC for higher limits.

rows: Bank- and app- set daily limits
Paying the price in equal monthly instalments (often on credit cards)
Short-term credit at checkout; late payment attracts charges
Pre-loaded cards for a fixed amount
Aadhaar Enabled Payment System — withdraw or deposit money at a banking agent with Aadhaar and fingerprint
One system to pay electricity, water, gas, mobile and DTH bills
RFID tag for automatic toll payment
A prepaid digital voucher for a specific purpose, such as a government health scheme
India's Central Bank Digital Currency, issued by RBI and tested in pilots since 2022

blocks.html: Note: Cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin are not legal tender in India. Their prices swing wildly, and they are often used in scams that promise quick profits. Stay away from such schemes.

rows: First purchase from a new site

lessons.title: 9.5 Benefits and risks of digital payments

blocks.html: Benefits: no need to carry cash; payments any time and from anywhere; automatic record of every transaction; less corruption and black money; direct benefit transfers reach citizens; cashback and offers.
Risks: fraud and phishing, failed transactions, dependence on network and battery, overspending, privacy of transaction data, and exclusion of people without smartphones or digital skills.

items.html: Never share your UPI PIN, card PIN, CVV, OTP or net-banking password.
You never need a PIN to receive money. If someone asks you to scan a QR code or enter your PIN to "receive" money, it is a fraud.
Check the payee's name on the screen before entering the PIN.
Use only official apps; never install "screen-sharing" apps at the request of a caller.
Set daily limits and turn off international or online card use when not needed.
Turn on SMS/email alerts and check your statements.
For a failed transaction, wait for the automatic reversal within the time RBI prescribes,

blocks.html: and use the app's or bank's complaint option. Do not search for "customer care numbers" on the internet.

items.html: Report fraud immediately on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in, and to your bank. The RBI

blocks.html: Ombudsman handles unresolved complaints against banks and payment companies.
Did you know? India processes more real-time digital payments than any other country, and UPI is now accepted in several other countries as well.
Aim: To understand payment methods and practise safe habits (no real money needed).

items.html: Read a receipt. With a parent, open the transaction history of a UPI app. Note the parts of a transaction: amount, payee name, UPI ID, date-time and UTR/reference number.
Compare methods. Make an Excel table comparing COD, debit card, credit card, net banking, UPI and wallet on speed, cost, safety and convenience.
NEFT, RTGS or IMPS? For each case, choose the best method: (a) ₹5 lakh for a house deposit today; (b) ₹1,500 to a friend at midnight; (c) monthly salary to 50 employees.
Spot the scam. Your teacher will show five payment-related messages (collect requests, QR codes, refund calls). Identify the frauds and explain why.
Family awareness. Teach one elder in your family the rule "PIN is only for paying, never for receiving" and write their response.
An e-payment system moves money electronically; it should be secure, convenient, fast, cheap, reliable and widely accepted.
A card payment involves the customer, merchant, issuing bank, acquiring bank, card network and payment gateway.
Methods include COD, debit and credit cards, net banking, UPI, wallets, NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, EMI, BNPL, AEPS, BBPS, FASTag, e-RUPI and the Digital Rupee.
UPI (NPCI, 2016) uses a UPI ID and PIN for instant 24 × 7 payments; UPI Lite, 123PAY and AutoPay extend it.
Never share PIN, OTP or CVV; a PIN is never needed to receive money; report fraud on 1930.
